title: Netlify Isn't Just a Static CDN: How Atomic Deploys, Edge Isolates, and Content-Addressed Storage Actually Work Under the Hood
why_read: A reasonably detailed architectural explainer on how Netlify's deployment and edge system actually works under the hood, going beyond the common oversimplified mental model of 'S3 plus CloudFront'.
analysis: The article explains Netlify's atomic deploys via content-addressed storage, arguing this avoids the common 'asset drift' problem where users load a mix of old and new files during a rolling deployment. It also touches on edge isolates (likely Deno-based) for fast cold starts and a distributed 'Smart CDN' routing design without central bottlenecks. This is useful conceptual grounding for engineers who use Netlify or similar platforms but have only a surface-level understanding of how zero-downtime deploys and content-addressing work. The technical depth seems solid for a 10-minute read, though it is vendor-specific and promotional in tone.
